dataPartitionPolicy.userDecision: Use GMBA outlines for data/graph preparation regions, keeping each whole whenever it is reasonably sized. Within oversized regions, prioritize and keep the most major through-highway cuts, then make the fewest additional lower-tier cuts needed. The user delegates the engineering size measure and accepts prompting for missing prepared-data downloads. Hikes crossing applied highway dividers are outside the accepted search scope, including pedestrian bridges and underpasses.
dataPartitionPolicy.status: Prepared and locally installed all five existing Washington Cascades sections on 2026-10-06 with no unavailable sections. dataPartitionPolicy.partitionTrigger: Keep a GMBA region whole up to 700,000 relevant consecutive OSM source-node pairs, before corridor compression. Count once per source segment regardless of walking direction; include admitted trails and road connectors. Duplicate source ways and unresolved barriers conservatively overcount. A cut requires both a currently oversized piece and a genuine available highway divider. The default is calibrated with real preparation and loaded-graph/search observations; it is a capacity proxy, not a guarantee for arbitrary future sources or query durations.
dataPartitionPolicy.cutSelection: Engineering default under the user's delegated choice: apply the size gate first. For an oversized GMBA region, retain all suitable through-freeway dividers, then choose the fewest additional approved lower-tier highway cuts needed to bring the pieces under the size threshold. Prefer more significant corridors and lower largest-piece workload when equally small selections are feasible. Do not cut a small region merely because a highway exists. Never introduce an artificial divider when an oversized piece has no suitable highway; report that unresolved preparation capacity instead.
proposedWorkflow: Identify a named GMBA region to add within supported coverage.

approved: Replace visible Repeat percentages with absolute Stem distance in search, rows, details and sorting. Stem is the one-way approach walked again on the return. Search steps by 1 mile, or 1 kilometer in metric.

Keep compact circular markers. All trailheads and numbered groups use charcoal and white; individual starts are hollow circles and the active one fills charcoal at the same size. No extra outer ring or focus decoration.

Use compact 28 px grouping circles with centered 13 px semibold tabular numbers, expanding only for larger counts. Asc/Desc is an underlined text control without a box.
stemUnitsAndMapDecision.supersedes: Earlier percentage repetition controls, separate saved-hike count/copy row, draft banners, added selection rings, active size changes, orange trailheads and blue route traces.
stemUnitsAndMapDecision.architecture: Shared unit formatting and exact editable-limit conversion live in the client units/SearchControls modules. validation.offline: 45 focused client, saved-route, query and whole-app checks pass. 62 engine/query/diversity checks pass, including independent exact-boundary, asymmetric-approach and same-stem/different-circuit cases. validation.browser: Saved real routes verified with imperial and metric search, rows, detail metrics and profile units; preference survives reload. Route inspection shows the burnt-orange stroke and distinct charcoal start; no browser errors.

routeOverviewDecision.approved: Show saved-route paths for comparing an area without panel hovering. Final user refinements: begin at zoom 9, increase muted strokes to 2–3 px, and use 95% opacity. Burnt orange identifies only a hovered or selected route.
routeOverviewDecision.architecture: A completed-only, revision-pinned paths endpoint sends unique referenced physical trail drawings within the view, without elevation data. Shared and returning sections draw once. The map retains one surrounding window, reuses it on short pans, aborts replaced requests and releases overview data below the threshold or on job changes. Hover/click hit testing reuses existing route inspection, with an 8 px target and no hover updates during panning. No new dependencies, schema, cache subsystem or search changes.

validation.offline: 42 focused client/store/whole-app checks pass, including viewport filtering, shared/return-path deduplication, preferred-only legacy drawings, completion gating, invalid bounds and unchanged geometry after source removal/restart. validation.browser: Real Bellingham-area results show a muted connected route network and one distinct burnt-orange inspected route at wider comparison scale. localContainerDelivery.approved: Keep local startup simple with one app container, automatic prepared-data acquisition and persistent jobs. Use GitHub Releases for prepared data; hikers never run preparation or configure catalogs.
localContainerDelivery.architecture: A two-stage Node 24 image runs the compiled app as a non-root user. Preparation remains the existing separate maintainer workflow.
localContainerDelivery.dataPolicy: Pin the catalog URL and SHA-256. Publish complete verified sections as flat assets with explicit download URLs, preserving local paths, IDs and bytes. gradeLimitsDecision.approved: Optional Grade limits checkbox and anchored popover, matching the compact search controls. Separate uphill/downhill threshold percentages, total allowed distance and longest stretch. Disabled by default; disabling retains draft values. No Settings changed indicator or hover fill. Inactive trigger is muted. Right-aligned single-line slope guidance: 5–10% moderate, 10–15% steep, 15–20% very steep and >20% extreme. No heading or dot separators.
gradeLimitsDecision.semantics: Signed grade uses the same centered 100 m window as profile hover, clipped at walk endpoints. Exact continuous threshold crossings measure total and longest exposure along the ordered walk, including return stems and trail joins. All limits apply before preferred start/direction selection and grouping. Unknown elevation never qualifies when grade limits are active. Immutable jobs retain their submitted grade limits.
gradeLimitsDecision.architecture: Shared pure elevation/grade module; enabled searches stream one section into compact distance/elevation pairs. Existing search preference and road proofs receive a grade predicate. No new dependency, prepared-data format or saved-result schema.
gradeLimitsDecision.validation: Build, typecheck, 102 focused checks (including the local HTTP download fixture with networking) and browser editing, enable/disable, retained values, Escape/focus and popover placement pass. Real Horse Lake searches consider all five starts: four hikes with initial limits and three with tighter 200 m total / 100 m longest budgets, about 17.3 seconds each. Independent Python 1 m integration of saved geometry verifies every returned budget. Evidence: .local-data/grade-review.json and .local-data/grade-review-strict.json. Existing six saved jobs remain available after local server restart. Maintained source: 10,170 lines across 57 files.
